items.title: Koei Tecmo reveals an 'AI chat RPG' built on Atelier Ryza
items.excerpt: Koei Tecmo unveils an 'AI chat RPG' built on Atelier Ryza, where an LLM drives free-form conversation with the character instead of authored dialogue trees. A mainstream publisher shipping generative dialogue as the product, not a demo.
items.rationale: First major publisher to ship LLM dialogue as the product itself rather than a tech demo — the clearest signal yet of how generative conversation reshapes narrative and character design.

items.title: Why new EU deepfake legislation means games need to be careful with real people and locations
items.excerpt: New EU deepfake rules put fresh constraints on games depicting real people and real places, with direct consequences for likeness capture, digital doubles and AI-assisted asset pipelines.
items.rationale: Directly actionable legal constraint on likeness capture, digital doubles and AI-generated environments — changes what art and tech teams can legally put in a build starting now.

items.title: Meet the workers dodging (and sabotaging) their employer's AI mandates
items.excerpt: Aftermath interviews workers quietly dodging, misdirecting and sabotaging their employers' AI mandates: sarcastic compliance, meeting boycotts, silent reversion to old methods. The internal politics of top-down AX rollouts, from the floor.
items.rationale: The ground-level view of how top-down AI mandates actually land inside creative teams — essential reading for anyone planning an AX rollout rather than announcing one.

items.title: Here's why game studios are moving beyond legacy version control
items.excerpt: Diversion pitches a version-control layer rebuilt for AI coding agents and mixed code/binary game projects, arguing studios shouldn't have to choose between Git-style tooling and artist-friendly asset workflows. Pipeline plumbing is where AI adoption actually breaks.
items.rationale: Concrete pipeline tooling: once coding agents start committing, version control for mixed code-and-binary art projects becomes the bottleneck — a workflow change teams can act on.

items.title: MMO life sim Seed's AI-powered avatars prove nothing shatters immersion quicker than crappy chatbot dialogue
items.excerpt: Klang's decade-in-development MMO Seed ships LLM-driven avatars, and PC Gamer finds the conversations useful as a tutorial layer but corrosive to immersion. A rare in-the-wild verdict on generative NPC dialogue as shipped design.
items.rationale: A rare hands-on verdict on generative NPC dialogue in a shipped game — the practical counterweight to the Atelier Ryza promise, showing where LLM characters help and where they break the fiction.
